Senses.Note: The weaving phrase describes closely connected back-and-forth work. Records apply it to verbal exchange, case commentary, and the literal metaphor of stitching a robe; the phrase does not by itself decide whether that work succeeds.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Thread coming, line going pictures sustained back-and-forth work whose parts are closely joined.
EvidenceBody: Dahui Zonggao caps the Baofu exchange with the line and says it manipulates the vital spirit. An unattributed verse says the coming thread and going line settle entanglement and weave intricate brocade from one shuttle. Yuanwu Keqin describes Danxia and Layman Pang's encounter as threading back and forth, half closing and half opening. Xingjiao Poyun uses the phrase while presenting a robe stitched where needle and wind cannot enter. These deployments preserve the weaving motion while distinguishing verbal and material applications.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The weaving image appraises tightly linked encounter moves and also appears in a robe presentation that makes its textile basis explicit.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: Back-and-forth threading may be praised, criticized, or merely described; the headword alone does not entail correctness or victory.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: All four use the same connected threading image; figurative encounter work and textile action remain intelligible as one lexical object.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: The alternate makes the reciprocal motion explicit without adding an evaluation.

ModifierControls.Finding: The paired textile nouns and opposed motion license a back-and-forth threading image, not generic verbosity.

FamilyControls.Finding: These are attested application domains, not separate definitions.
